learning_objective: 🎯 Trace the incredible journey of a child's early years—from basic survival needs to the rapid physical and mental milestones of growth!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: For an infant to survive, they need basic care: proper nutrition (breast milk), warmth, hygiene, immunisation against diseases, and a safe environment.
Growth refers to physical changes in size, weight, and height (it can be measured). Development refers to the increase in skills, understanding, and complexity (like learning to speak or walk).
This is the control over body movements. Gross Motor Skills involve large muscles (crawling, walking, jumping). Fine Motor Skills involve small muscles (holding a pencil, picking up a bead).
Cognitive development is how a child's brain learns to think, remember, and solve problems. Language development goes from cooing and babbling to forming complete sentences.
These are average ages when a child is expected to achieve a certain skill (e.g., sitting up at 6 months, walking at 12 months). However, every child has their own unique pace.

fun_activity.title: 🏃 Gross vs. Fine Motor Test
fun_activity.instructions: Try jumping on one leg for 10 seconds (Gross Motor Skill). Then, try to pick up a single grain of rice using a pair of tweezers or chopsticks (Fine Motor Skill). Feel how different muscles work!

exam_tips: 📌 Always know the exact difference between Growth (quantitative) and Development (qualitative).
📌 Be able to give 2 examples each for Gross Motor Skills and Fine Motor Skills.
📌 Remember that development proceeds from head to toe (Cephalocaudal) and center to outwards (Proximodistal).
quick_recap: ⭐ Proper nutrition and immunisation are critical for a child's survival.
⭐ Development is a continuous, lifelong process.
⭐ A loving, stimulating environment accelerates cognitive and language development.
